memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And take some blood from the altar and some of the anointing oil and sprinkle it on Aaron and his garments and on his sons and their garments. Then he and his sons and their garments will be consecrated." - Exodus 29:21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Blood from the altar and anointing oil are sprinkled together on Aaron, his sons, and their garments. Both elements appear side by side — the blood that atones and the oil that anoints. Cleansing and empowering, forgiveness and equipping, arriving in the same moment.

We sometimes separate these. Some believers focus entirely on forgiveness and never expect God to empower them for anything. Others chase experiences of power while neglecting the cleansing that makes them fit to serve. God joins the two. He forgives us in order to commission us, and He equips those He has cleansed.

Notice also that the whole household is consecrated together — Aaron and his sons, all of them included. God was not setting apart an individual but a family for His service. There is encouragement here for anyone praying for their household. God works generationally, and He delights to claim families for Himself. Whether you are the first believer in your family or the fourth, ask God to consecrate your whole house to His service.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I holding cleansing and empowering together, or focusing on only one?
What would it look like to pray for my whole household to be set apart for God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You cleanse and equip Your people in the same breath. Wash me and empower me for Your service, and set apart my whole household to belong to You. Amen.
